# inbox.dog

> Gmail OAuth in 3 API calls. Skip the audit. Ship today.

## The problem

Gmail API requires restricted OAuth scopes. Google mandates a CASA Tier 2 security audit before granting access. That audit costs thousands of dollars, takes weeks, and requires ongoing compliance. Most teams can't justify it.

## The solution

inbox.dog already passed the CASA Tier 2 audit. Use it as an OAuth proxy: your app redirects users to inbox.dog, they authenticate with Google, you get back standard Gmail API tokens. inbox.dog is never in the data path after that — tokens go directly to gmail.googleapis.com.

## Why use this instead of self-hosting

- **No audit**: inbox.dog's CASA Tier 2 certification covers your app. You skip the entire audit process.
- **3 API calls**: Create key → redirect user → exchange code. That's it.
- **$0.10 per flow**: 10 free credits on signup. Token refresh is free. You only pay when users authenticate.
- **Open source (MIT)**: Full codebase at https://github.com/acoyfellow/inbox.dog. Self-host when you outgrow it — or never.
- **MCP native**: AI agents connect via `https://inbox.dog/mcp` with automatic OAuth discovery. Works with Open Claw, Claude, and any MCP client.

## When to self-host instead

Self-host if you're a platform doing 10,000+ OAuth flows/month, need to own the entire auth chain, or want to pass your own CASA audit. The code is MIT-licensed and runs on Cloudflare Workers.

## Quick start

```bash
# 1. Create API key
curl -s -X POST https://inbox.dog/api/keys \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "my-app"}'

# Returns: { client_id, client_secret, credits: 10 }

# 2. Redirect user to authenticate
# GET https://inbox.dog/oauth/authorize?client_id=YOUR_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_CALLBACK&scope=email

# 3. Exchange code for tokens
curl -s -X POST https://inbox.dog/oauth/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"code": "AUTH_CODE", "client_id": "YOUR_ID", "client_secret": "YOUR_SECRET"}'

# Returns: { access_token, refresh_token, email }
# access_token works directly with gmail.googleapis.com
```

## MCP (for AI agents)

Endpoint: `https://inbox.dog/mcp`

Tools: read_emails, read_email, send_email, search_emails, get_profile

Auth is automatic — MCP clients discover OAuth endpoints via `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, register dynamically, and run a PKCE flow. No config beyond the URL.

## Scopes

| Scope      | Access                       |
|------------|------------------------------|
| email      | Read-only (default)          |
| email:send | Send only                    |
| email:full | Read, send, modify           |

## Pricing

| | Cost |
|---|---|
| OAuth flow | $0.10 |
| Token refresh | Free |
| Signup credits | 10 free |
| Self-host | Free (MIT) |

## npm package

```
npm install inbox.dog
```

```typescript
import { InboxDog } from "inbox.dog";
const dog = new InboxDog();
const key = await dog.createKey("my-app");
const url = dog.getAuthUrl({ clientId: key.client_id, redirectUri: "http://localhost:3000/callback" });
const tokens = await dog.exchangeCode(code, key.client_id, key.client_secret);
```
